extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians and readers of comedy memoirs / fans of Steve Martin
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts principles and standards, as presented in a Steve Martin memoir review, for developing, evaluating, and sustaining a career in stand-up comedy. Focuses on what made Martin successful: originality, long-term craft, risk-taking, and managing the costs of fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term commitment / time investment
rubrics_metrics.description: I did stand-up comedy for 18 years. Ten of those years were spent learning, four years were spent refining, and four were spent in wild success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success is framed as the result of many years (decades) of work rather than a short sprint. Evaluations should account for multi-year development phases (learning, refining, breakthrough). Examples: Martin's 18-year timeline; expect lengthy periods with little external validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of material
rubrics_metrics.description: There could be nothing that made the audience feel they weren’t seeing something utterly new; he had to write everything in the act himself and expunge any line with a vague feeling of familiarity or provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original authorship of lines and concepts is a core standard: borrowed or familiar material must be removed. The reviewer emphasizes eliminating gag-book one-liners and well-known bits to make the act feel 'utterly new.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage to abandon safe material / risk-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: He showed immense courage in being willing to let go of the safety net of an act that was guaranteed to perform well for one of his own ideas, material that would develop slowly and flop many times before finding threads that were worth keeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willingness to risk immediate success (and cash) for long-term growth is valued. Practically: intentionally trying new material that may fail publicly, and tolerating flops as part of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stable jobs to support development
rubrics_metrics.description: He used other jobs to give him stability while he developed himself as an artist but knew when it was time to cast off that security and jump into the sea of the unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing financial/security work with creative practice is recommended. Use steady employment to fund artistic development, but maintain readiness to take the leap when the act is ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-disciplinary study and varied influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Martin's artistic vision was informed by magic, juggling, banjo playing, and studies in literature, poetry, the visual arts, music, philosophy, and the avant-garde scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad study across arts and intellectual disciplines is presented as a way to develop a unique voice. Guidance: draw on diverse traditions (music, poetry, philosophy, magic) to inform comedic approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-time audience feedback as truth metric
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something incredibly lonely and terrifying about presenting your art in real-time to an audience where the laughs don't lie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live audience reaction is treated as an honest, immediate gauge of what works. Evaluate material primarily by whether it produces the intended reaction in performance contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative development and refinement of material
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing comic material is difficult and takes a long time... 'Because I knew it took me ten years to get this much material.' 'For the next eight years I rolled it up a hill like Sisyphus.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should be iteratively tested and refined over many performances. Expect slow accrual of usable bits; value processes that nurture gradual improvement (workshopping, scrapping, reworking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discarding borrowed or imitation material
rubrics_metrics.description: Any line or idea with even a vague feeling of familiarity or provenance had to be expunged... I would lose another prime gag I had lifted... The thought of losing all this material was depressing because... I was now starting from almost zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concrete criterion: remove imitative bits even at the cost of shrinking the act temporarily. The reviewer uses Martin's painful pruning as an example of necessary creative discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perseverance and incremental progress (not heroic leaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: The course was more plodding than heroic: I did not strive valiantly against doubters but took incremental steps studded with a few intuitive leaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value steady persistence and small cumulative advances over narratives of sudden triumph. Assess progress by consistent incremental gains rather than one-off dramatic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of success: managing fame and isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: He speaks of how much difficulty he still faced in terms of finding ways to keep being original and how isolating it was to play for a crowd of 45,000 people... being too famous to even attempt walking down the streets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate not just breakthrough but sustainability and personal costs. Consider whether success preserves creative vitality or induces isolation, and whether the performer has strategies to cope with fame's adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowing when to transition or leave
rubrics_metrics.description: In the end, I turned away from stand-up with a tired swivel of my head and never looked back... writing this book felt more like a biography of someone I used to be instead of an autobiography of who I am today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful career includes awareness of transitions—recognizing when to move to new projects or leave a medium. Assessments should consider whether the artist can redefine themselves and pursue other phases productively.
